thread:
ryan (docs): Noticed inconsistency in API ref for GET /v1/records. Param `include_metadata` is documented as a string enum ("yes"/"no") in examples, but runtime expects a boolean and the response schema includes `request_id` that docs don't show. This caused confusion in the JS SDK examples.

ellen (eng-api): We toggled to boolean to simplify parsing. The enum string was an old pattern from the UI. Good catch. Also, we added `request_id` last month for tracing — docs missed it.

ryan (docs): Current example: GET /v1/records?include_metadata=yes
Docs example body shows records array only. Runtime returns: 200 and JSON { "records": [...], "metadata": {...}, "request_id": "r_abc123" } when include_metadata=true.

harry (sdk): SDK examples and the fetch helper were showing query param as string. I'll update snippets to use boolean in query or body and add code to surface request_id in responses for users.

ci-bot: docs-pr/1769999999-records-include-metadata-boolean queued (lint + snippet checks).

ryan (docs): Proposal: 1) Update examples to use include_metadata=true (boolean). 2) Add response example showing metadata and request_id. 3) Add a small migration note: old string values supported for one release. 4) Update Node/Python snippet to read request_id from response and recommend logging it for support.

ellen (eng-api): Approved. We'll keep the string shim for one release and add a server-side deprecation header when string values are used.

harry (sdk): Opening SDK PRs and linking to the docs PR. I'll include code snippet: const includeMetadata = opts.includeMetadata === true || opts.includeMetadata === 'yes'; // temporary compat.

ryan (docs): PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5123 - includes examples, migration note, and updated snippets. Requesting quick review from eng-api and sdk.
